task.description:
Implement design section 10 of lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASSed it with zero BLOCKERs -- handoffs/WF03-ISS0480-20260905/step-02b-code-design-validator.json). Read section 10 in full (subsections 10.0-10.7) before writing any code -- it is the normative source for every module/config/signature you create. Do NOT re-derive the design yourself; implement exactly what section 10.3's normative subsections (10.3.1-10.3.4) specify, and resolve section 10.7's open questions using your own engineering judgement where they are flagged as implementer-discretion (naming/organization choices with no behavior difference) -- they are explicitly NOT ambiguous about WHAT ships, only about minor implementation choices.

Summary of what ships (full detail is in the design, this is not a substitute for reading it): a new test-only Ecto.Repo module (Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo per the design's naming) with its own pool/adapter config, and `Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1` changed so its Sandbox.mode/2 call targets this new repo instead of Letflow.Repo -- via Ecto.Repo.put_dynamic_repo/1, exactly as section 10.3.2's seam describes. `provisioned_tenant!/1`'s public @spec, opts() type, and return shape must NOT change (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently confirmed this is the design's own claim and it is checkable -- verify it stays true after your own edit, not just before). Zero edits to any of the 46 existing call sites. config/test.exs gets a new sibling config block per 10.3.4. scripts/test_parallel.sh's TEST_POOL_SIZE formula is extended by the fixed PROVISIONING_POOL_SIZE=2 term per 10.2.2/10.3.4 -- do not accidentally make this term core-count-derived; the design and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's independent arithmetic both depend on it staying a FIXED constant.

Open question 10.7 OQ-6 (application_name tag interaction with ISS-0110's TenantSchemaReaper liveness guard) requires you to check test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex's actual source before finalizing the new repo's connection config -- do not skip this; a wrongly-tagged or untagged new pool's connections could either falsely trigger or fail to trigger ISS-0110's own concurrent-invocation guard, which would be a regression against an already-resolved issue, not a new defect but a real regression risk this open question exists to head off.

After implementing: compile clean (`mix compile --warnings-as-errors`), and run the scoped set of tests this change can plausibly affect (test/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs, test/support/tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs, test/letflow/row_approval_test.exs, test/letflow/definitions/pack_update_migration_test.exs, and at least 2-3 of the 46 TenantFixture-calling test files including the 2 already-async ones) before handing to REVIEWER -- do not wait for TEST-DESIGNER's regression test to be the first signal something is broken. This is Unblock-Everything territory (core-directives.md): if your own implementation reveals a design gap CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's static read couldn't have caught, report it in result.issues and consider whether it needs a rework note back to CODE-DESIGNER (do not silently patch around a real design gap).

SECURITY-REVIEWER note: this touches test-support infrastructure only (test/support/, config/test.exs, scripts/test_parallel.sh) -- no lib/letflow/ production code, no migration, no tenant-data API path. State plainly in your own result whether you believe this is in or out of SECURITY-REVIEWER's scope so ORCH can route correctly; do not assume out-of-scope without stating the reasoning (core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence: a safety/gate rule is never silently skipped).

provisioned_tenant!/1's Sandbox.mode/2 call redirected via put_dynamic_repo/1 per section 10.3.2, with default dynamic repo correctly restored to Letflow.Repo afterward (per the design's own 3-wrap-point requirement, OQ-7)

result.summary:
Implemented design §10 exactly as specified (§10.3.1-10.3.4): new test-only Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo (test/support/provisioning_repo.ex, use Ecto.Repo otp_app: :letflow, adapter: Ecto.Adapters.Postgres, no custom functions, matching §10.3.1 byte-for-byte). provisioned_tenant!/1's Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) line removed entirely (§10.3.2 step 1); a new private with_provisioning_repo/1 wraps every provisioning-related Repo call (Tenant insert, provision_schema!/2, assert_schema_complete!/2, teardown/2) in Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto) + Repo.put_dynamic_repo(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo), restoring the previous dynamic repo in an `after` block (OQ-7, exception-safe). @spec provisioned_tenant!(opts()) :: tenant_fixture(), opts() type, and return shape re-verified byte-for-byte unchanged after the edit (diffed against pre-edit source, not assumed). Zero edits to any of the 46 existing call sites' own files. config/test.exs got a sibling config block (§10.3.4: same database/hostname/port/MIX_TEST_PARTITION scoping as Letflow.Repo, pool_size: 2 fixed, identical application_name tag-derivation logic). scripts/test_parallel.sh's TEST_POOL_SIZE formula extended with a `PROVISIONING_POOL_SIZE=2` bash constant subtracted as `N * PROVISIONING_POOL_SIZE` from budget (§10.2.2) -- confirmed it is a literal, not derived from nproc/N. test/test_helper.exs starts Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo.start_link() before ExUnit.start() (§10.3.3 test-only boot sequencing, no change to lib/letflow/application.ex).

OQ-6 finding (required check against tenant_schema_reaper.ex's real source, not assumed): read test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex directly. concurrent_invocation_present?/2 (lines 299-310) counts DISTINCT application_name TAGS via `SELECT application_name FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE application_name LIKE 'letflow_mixtest_%' AND application_name <> $1 (own_tag)`, then treats any row whose group suffix differs from its own as a hazard. It has no per-connection-count or one-connection-per-test-process assumption anywhere -- it is purely tag-based. Since config/test.exs gives ProvisioningRepo's connections the IDENTICAL application_name derivation as Letflow.Repo's (same System.pid()/TEST_PARALLEL_GROUP inputs), every ProvisioningRepo connection reports the exact same tag as this invocation's own Letflow.Repo connections and is therefore excluded from the 'other invocation' set by the `<> $1` filter alone -- it never even reaches the group-suffix comparison. The design's own assumption in OQ-6 holds; no design update needed for this open question.

mix format: clean. mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force: clean, 190 files, zero warnings, twice (before and after the fix below).

GENUINE DESIGN GAP FOUND DURING SCOPED TESTING (not silently patched around, per task instruction): §10.4 claims 'every existing call site's own source... requires zero edits to keep working exactly as before' -- this is FALSIFIED by real execution for 2 of the 46 files. Root cause: §10.3.2 step 1 removes provisioned_tenant!/1's side effect of leaving Letflow.Repo's sandbox pool in :auto mode for the rest of the calling test. That side effect was never merely internal -- at least 2 of the 46 call sites have their OWN hand-rolled helpers that call Letflow.Repo directly (bare `Repo.query!`/`Repo.delete_all` against the provisioned schema) and structurally depend on Letflow.Repo already being in :auto mode when they run, because before this fix ALL of provisioning ran on Letflow.Repo's own connection. Confirmed both are genuine regressions, not pre-existing: verified against the unmodified tree via `git stash` (baseline: 14/14 and 12/12 pass respectively) before and after my change on the same commit.

1. test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs: 8/14 pass (was 14/14 baseline). All 6 failures are the identical shape -- `on_exit(fn -> hard_cleanup(fixture.tenant_id) end)` (test file line 422) calls its own `hard_cleanup/1` helper (line 426-434), which does bare `Repo.query!(DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS ... CASCADE)` against Letflow.Repo from the on_exit process (not a descendant of the test process, no ambient checkout) -- this needed :auto-mode auto-checkout to work, which no longer happens: `** (EXIT) shutdown: "owner ... exited"`.
2. test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs: 3/12 pass (was 12/12 baseline). Worse than a teardown edge case -- this file's own helpers (`drop_schema!`, `schema_exists?`, `sandbox_process_definition_ids`, lines ~100-160) all call bare `Repo.query!` against Letflow.Repo directly, and its own moduledoc explicitly documents relying on `provisioned_tenant/0`'s (i.e. TenantFixture's) 'same sandbox :auto switch' side effect. One failure changes a mechanism-(c)-shaped assertion's own expected error tuple ({:error, :provision_failed} expected, {:error, {:transaction_failed, exception}} observed) because a real second provisioning call against Letflow.Repo now hits a connection in :manual mode instead of :auto.

Blast radius is otherwise clean and precisely bounded: ran 172 additional tests across 11 more TenantFixture-calling files with zero unexpected failures -- the ACTUAL ISS-0480 victims (test/letflow/row_approval_test.exs, test/letflow/definitions/pack_update_migration_test.exs: both fully pass) plus the 2 already-async files (secrets_test.exs, webhooks_test.exs), tenant_fixture_dispatch_test.exs, tenant_provisioning_test.exs, identity/user_test.exs, identity/group_test.exs, identity/tenant_role_test.exs, role_registry_test.exs, engine_sub_process_test.exs, audit_test.exs, definitions/store_test.exs, tenant_onboarding_test.exs (combined: 65 + 43 + 64 = 172 passed, 0 failed). The core ISS-0480 structural mechanism is proven correct and working; the gap is narrowly confined to 2 files whose own local helpers made an undocumented assumption about provisioned_tenant!/1's side effects on Letflow.Repo, an assumption the design's §10.4 'zero call-site edits' claim did not anticipate and cannot be true for these 2 files without either (a) those 2 files' own helpers being edited to call Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto) or use ProvisioningRepo themselves, which is a call-site edit the design explicitly said would not be needed, or (b) a design-level compatibility mechanism I am not authorized to invent unilaterally (e.g. any form of Letflow.Repo :auto-mode compatibility shim would risk reintroducing exactly the ISS-0480 hazard this fix removes). Not silently patched -- reporting per task's explicit instruction.

SECURITY-REVIEWER scope judgement: OUT of scope. This diff touches only test/support/ (tenant_fixture.ex, provisioning_repo.ex), test/test_helper.exs, config/test.exs, and scripts/test_parallel.sh -- zero changes to lib/letflow/ production code, zero migrations, zero API route/response-shaping code, zero secrets/config keys read at runtime by production paths (LETFLOW_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY and friends are untouched). No tenant-data API path is touched; this is test-only provisioning-connection plumbing. Stating this reasoning explicitly per core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence rather than assuming silently.

issues.description: Design §10.4's claim 'every existing call site's own source... requires zero edits to keep working exactly as before' is false for 2 of the 46 TenantFixture call sites: test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs (8/14 pass, was 14/14 on unmodified tree) and test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs (3/12 pass, was 12/12 on unmodified tree). Both files have their own local helpers that call Letflow.Repo directly (DROP SCHEMA, information_schema queries, a deliberate second real provisioning call) and structurally depend on provisioned_tenant!/1's now-removed side effect of leaving Letflow.Repo's sandbox pool in :auto mode. §10.3.2 step 1 (removing that Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) call) is necessary for the ISS-0480 fix to work at all, so this is not implementer error -- it is an interaction CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's static read could not have caught (only real execution surfaces it). Needs a CODE-DESIGNER decision: either declare these 2 files' own helpers in-scope for an edit (call Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Test.ProvisioningRepo, :auto) or route through put_dynamic_repo themselves before their own Repo calls), or specify some other compatibility mechanism, revising §10.4's 'zero call-site edits' claim explicitly rather than leaving it standing as false.

result.next_action: ORCH: the core ISS-0480 structural fix is implemented, compiles clean, and is verified working (172/172 tests passed across the actual ISS-0480 victims, the 2 already-async files, and 9 more TenantFixture-calling files). One BLOCKER-severity design gap (above) affects exactly 2 of 46 files and needs a CODE-DESIGNER decision before this can pass to REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER as a clean, fully-working change -- route a rework note to CODE-DESIGNER for §10.4's call-site-edit claim, scoped narrowly to these 2 named files, rather than re-opening §10's core mechanism (which is proven sound). Recommend NOT routing to SECURITY-REVIEWER/REVIEWER until this is resolved, since 'zero call-site edits' was itself one of CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's independently-verified PASS claims (step-02b) and is now known false.
